Article Title: Mahua slams rebel TMC MPs over delay in responding to disqualification notices
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Wednesday slammed the party's rebel MPs for seeking additional time to respond to notices issued to them by the Lok Sabha secretariat.While talking to reporters, Mahua said that the rebel MPs' inability to respond within the stipulated period shows that they know they are in the wrong."We have filed 20 disqualification petitions against MPs who were elected on TMC tickets but joined hands with the BJP . The Lok Sabha Secretariat sent notices last week to them asking them to reply within seven days. The deadline is over, but they could not reply. Now they have sought another two-three weeks," Mahua said."We had written to the Lok Sabha Speaker in June. Why were they unable to reply in two months? Why does it take you more than one week to reply? If you ask me, I will not take so much time to reply," she added."The wigs and masks have come off. Their shamelessness and betrayal are for everyone to see," she said.This comes a day after TMC MP Sudip Bandhopadhyay said that the rebel MPs had sought an additional three weeks from the Lok Sabha secretariat to respond to notices issued on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification.Last month, the Lok Sabha secretariat had issued notices to the MPs after the Supreme Court agreed to hear Abhishek Banerjee's plea seeking an expeditious decision by Speaker Om Birla on the disqualification petitions.The rebel MPs are understood to be consulting lawyers before submitting their replies, with the additional time sought by them potentially extending the legal battle over their continuation as members of the House.The dispute is part of a larger political confrontation within the TMC following the party's defeat in the West Bengal assembly polls earlier this year, with the dissident camp challenging the authority of the leadership headed by party supremo Mamata Banerjee.The 20 Lok Sabha MPs subsequently aligned themselves with the NCPI and joined the BJP-led NDA, prompting the TMC leadership to initiate disqualification proceedings under the anti-defection law.
Article Summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra slams party's rebel MPs for seeking additional time to respond to notices issued to them by the Lok Sabha secretariat. Mahua said that the rebel MPs' inability to respond within the stipulated period shows that they know they are in the wrong.

Article Title: 'They are from his film fan base': Congress MLA brushes aside TVK’s 'Vijay for PM' pitch
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert on Wednesday dismissed ally TVK’s projection of its leader, C Joseph Vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, saying TVK leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to Vijay’s past as an actor.“They are TVK MLAs, they are all still in the fan basis. They have come from a fan--film industries as a fan basis. Definitely, they will be saying that,” Cuthbert told reporters in Chennai.She added that, politically, the leaders had taken a “stern decision” that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi would be the candidate for the prime minister’s post in 2029.Cuthbert’s remarks come amid growing differences over the political positioning of the two parties, with TVK leaders repeatedly projecting Vijay as a possible national leader.TVK leader and Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier asserted that the country’s top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.Responding to the remarks by TVK leaders, Congress leader and state Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar warned that the two Congress ministers in the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government would resign if the Vijay-led party did not accept Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate.The Congress ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and extended support to TVK, which emerged as the single-largest party but fell short of the majority mark. The Congress backed TVK along with the VCK, IUML, CPI and CPI(M), with the stated condition that “communal forces” be kept out of the government.Vijay launched TVK in February 2024, becoming the latest Tamil film star to enter state politics.The Congress last led a government at the Centre from 2004 to 2014.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert dismissed ally TVK’s projection of its leader, C Joseph Vijay, as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. She said TVK leaders were making the claim as “fans” of the chief minister, a reference to Vijay's past as an actor. The Congress ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections in April and extended support to TVK.

Article Title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs
Article Text:
TMC rebel MPs after attending the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) Parliamentary Party Meeting (ANI photo)

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI and sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that lays down the anti-defection framework.Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.In a post on X, TMC Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra shared the photo of one of the notices issued to rebel MPs and said, “Cover up caught out!” Highlighting that TMC had filed 20 disqualification petitions in June, Moitra said, “Speaker LS did nothing except give them better seats at our expense. SG Tushar Mehta in Court said the Speaker had issued notices. Notice dated Aug 25th -- exact date of hearing!”On Tuesday, Supreme Court sought a response from Lok Sabha Speaker’s office on time-bound adjudication of TMC’s petition seeking disqualification of rebel MPs who broke away from the party after its electoral debacle in West Bengal, even as Abhishek Banerjee accused Speaker Om Birla of “deliberate inaction”.The SC also issued notices to the 20 rebel MPs: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachna Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Abu Teher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Kalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.In his petition, Abhishek Banerjee told the court on Tuesday that he had lodged the disqualification petition against the rebel MPs on June 18 and complained that despite the lapse of two months, no meaningful progress has been made on its adjudication.The continuing delay in the adjudication process is impacting democratic governance, he said.In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June. Banerjee had earlier met Birla on July 27 in Parliament urging him to expedite his decision on the pending petitions.
Article Summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI. The notices sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification.

Article Title: MP govt denies nod to prosecute cabinet minister Kunwar Vijay Shah over controversial remarks on Col Sofiya Qureshi
Article Text:
Army officer Colonel Sofiya Qureshi (L) and senior cabinet minister Kunwar Vijay Shah (R)

No sanction as no one filed any complaint yet: MP on Vijay Shah case





BHOPAL: MP govt has finalised a five-point reply explaining its decision not to grant sanction to prosecute senior cabinet minister Kunwar Vijay Shahover his controversial remarks on Army officer Colonel Sofiya Qureshi, who gained prominence during the media briefings on Operation Sindoor The reply is likely to be submitted before the Supreme Court in the next few days after being vetted by legal experts, the chief secretary and the chief minister’s office.The state cabinet headed by chief minister Mohan Yadav had on Aug 25 decided against granting sanction to prosecute Shah. The recommendation was subsequently sent to governor Mangubhai Patel, who approved it late Monday.The govt’s response, prepared after the governor endorsed the cabinet decision, states that no person came forward to lodge a complaint against Shah following his controversial remarks. It also argues that the minister did not name Col Sofiya Qureshi in his statement, subsequently apologised several times, and did not intend to insult anyone.Also read | Supreme Court in no mood to condone Madhya Pradesh minister in Col Sofiya Qureshi case Shah’s remarks neither disturbed communal harmony nor were made with any such intention, the govt further reasons.On Monday, additional solicitor general K M Nataraj, appearing for the state govt, had informed an SC bench headed by CJI Surya Kant that the SIT had completed its probe in the matter and a chargesheet would be filed once the sanction for prosecution, pending before the competent authority, was received.Shah came under fire after a video showed him making objectionable remarks against Col Qureshi in May 2025. The MP high court, taking suo motu cognisance, rebuked him for using “language of the gutters” and ordered police to file an FIR against him on charges of promoting enmity and hatred.On May 28, 2025, the SC ordered the closure of proceedings before the high court, saying it was now looking into the matter, and asked for a status report from the SIT constituted by the MP govt.After drawing severe condemnation, Shah expressed regret. However, on July 28 last year, the top court pulled up Shah for not placing a public apology over his remarks on record against Col Qureshi, saying he was “testing the court’s patience”. The minister subsequently apologised repeatedly.
Article Summary: Madhya Pradesh govt has finalised a five-point reply explaining its decision not to grant sanction to prosecute senior cabinet minister Kunwar Vijay Shah. The reply is likely to be submitted before the Supreme Court in the next few days. Shah came under fire after a video showed him making objectionable remarks against Col Qureshi in May 2025.

Article Title: Madras HC dismisses MK Stalin’s plea challenging TVK MLA’s Kolathur victory
Article Text:
The Madras HC has ruled against M K Stalin's plea disputing V S Babu's election win, which alleged EVM errors and inconsistencies post-counting





CHENNAI: Madras high court on Thursday dismissed as not maintainable a plea by DMK chief M K Stalin seeking to nullify the victory of TVK MLA V S Babu from the Kolathur assembly constituency. The plea was moved on the grounds of malfunctioning, mismatch, and discrepancies in the electronic voting machines (EVMs) during post-counting verification.The first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan passed the order on Thursday.Stalin had sought 100% counting of the VVPAT and checking and verification of all the 286 electronic voting machines used in the constituency.According to Stalin, he submitted an application for the post-counting checking and verification of the EVMs on May 7. But ECI conducted the exercise only from July 29 after a 45 days-delay.Supreme Court has mandated the ECI to hold the post-counting checking and verification of 5% of the EVMs used in a constituency. Total 14 machines were to be checked, and three of the four machines in the first batch were not functioning; so, another four were selected, of them one was not functioning, he said.He added that since ECI held the check after 45 days’ delay, he could not file an election petition and so the bar under Article 329 of the Constitution will not apply in this case.ECI submitted that the remedy for the petitioner lies in the election petition under section 80 of the Representation of the People Act and not a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution.They noted that there is a bar on such petitions as per Article 329 (B) of the Constitution and that the petitioner should have approached the ECI before the lapse of the 45 days for holding the post-counting check.
Article Summary: Stalin had sought 100% counting of the VVPAT and checking and verification of all the 286 electronic voting machines used in the constituency. The first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan passed the order.

Article Title: RG Kar rape-murder case: Absconding ex-chief of Panihati Municipality Somnath Dey arrested in Bengaluru
Article Text:
Panihati Municipality Chairman Somnath Dey





KOLKATA: A special team of Bengal Police arrested former Panihati Municipality chairman Somnath Dey in Bengaluru in the early hours of Thursday for his alleged role in the hurried cremation of the RG Kar rape and murder victim and the alleged destruction of evidence.Dey had been absconding, repeatedly changing locations and using multiple phone numbers after Khardah police station registered an FIR based on a complaint filed by the victim’s family on Aug 10.Dey’s name was found on the cremation ground requisition documents. Police will bring him to Bengal on transit remand, produce him before the Barrackpore court and then take him to Khardah police station for questioning to probe the alleged conspiracy and the instructions under which he acted.The victim’s family alleged that Dey misused his administrative power and influence to bypass legal and social procedures and arrange a hurried cremation, with the aim of destroying crucial evidence and disrupting the murder investigation.The Aug 10 FIR followed a directive from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari to the Barrackpore Police Commissionerate during an Aug 9 memorial meeting at Panihati to examine the events at the cremation ground.Dey is the third person arrested in connection with the FIR. Former Panihati MLA Nirmal Ghosh was arrested at a hotel near Puri in Odisha, while former councillor and neighbour Sanjib Mukhopadhyay was arrested at a house in Chinar Park, Kolkata.Both were granted bail in this case, although Ghosh remains in jail in connection with a separate case.
Article Summary: Dey had been absconding, repeatedly changing locations and using multiple phone numbers. Victim’s family alleged that Dey misused his administrative power and influence to bypass legal and social procedures. Police will bring him to Bengal on transit remand, produce him before the Barrackpore court and then take him to Khardah police station for questioning.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu assembly unanimously passes resolution to recognise Tamil as principal language of Madras high court
Article Text:
The TN assembly on Thursday unanimously adopted a resolution, moved by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.

(With PTI inputs)





CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the central government to recognise Tamil as the principal language of the Madras high court Chief minister C Joseph Vijay moved the resolution on Thursday, saying the demand was not intended to oppose or diminish the importance of any other language.The resolution received support from lawmakers across political parties, including the opposition DMK.During the debate, legislators recalled the history of the demand and highlighted efforts by their respective leaders to have Tamil recognised as a language of proceedings in the high court.After the debate, Speaker JCD Prabhakar announced that the resolution had been adopted unanimously.
Article Summary: The Tamil Nadu assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the central government to recognise Tamil as the principal language of the Madras high court. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay moved the resolution on Thursday, saying the demand was not intended to oppose or diminish the importance of any other language.

Article Title: Rahul or Vijay for PM? Congress-TVK rift talk grows after MLA’s seat shift
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay

NEW DELHI: Speculation over differences between Congress and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu grew on Monday after Congress MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the opposition benches in the state assembly.This comes a day after state tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the state cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Speaking at an event in Kanyakumari on Saturday, Kumar said Rahul Gandhi would become the Prime Minister in 2029.The remarks came amid statements by TVK leaders projecting party chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as a potential contender for the PM's post. TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier said the country's top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan questioned why the Congress continued to be part of the TVK government despite the differences over the prime ministerial candidate."Repeated assertions by multiple TVK Ministers even inside on the floor of the Tamil Nadu Assembly touting their leader as a probable Prime Minister is an outright rejection of the failed and dismal leadership of Rahul Gandhi by the TVK.Now, what is preventing the opportunistic Congress party from coming out of the cabinet of the TVK government? Article Title: Mira Bhayander-Vasai Virar crime branch busts drug manufacturing unit in Uttar Pradesh; 69.7kg mephedrone worth Rs 139 crore seized
Article Text:
A total of 21 accused have been arrested so far

Mira Road:





The Mira Bhayander-Vasai Virar crime branch, probing a drug network operating from Nalasopara, has raided a mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit in Manda in Prayagraj district, Uttar Pradesh , and recovered 52kg of the party drug.Police commissioner Niket Kaushik said the manufacturing unit in UP had been operating for the past six months and the accused had allegedly sold around 300kg of MD during this period.In June, Tulinj police arrested two men for allegedly selling MD. The probe was later transferred to Crime Branch Unit 4. A team led by senior inspector Pramod Badakh traced the drug network and found that the accused were operating manufacturing units in Gujarat and UP. But before police could raid the Gujarat unit, the accused allegedly dismantled it.So far, 21 people have been arrested and 69.8kg of mephedrone worth around Rs 139 crore seized in the case.One of the arrested accused is Mohammad Haseeb Siddiqui alias Ejaz Merchant (36), an engineer with a BE degree, who was allegedly involved in supplying MD in Mumbai, said senior inspector Badakh.
Article Summary: Police commissioner Niket Kaushik said the manufacturing unit in UP had been operating for the past six months. The accused had allegedly sold around 300kg of MD during this period. A total of 21 people have been arrested and 69.8kg of mephedrone worth around Rs 139 crore seized in the case.

Article Title: ​Govt delegation delays its visit to meet Jarange
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





The govt delegation led by cabinet sub-committee chairperson and BJP minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil on Tuesday delayed its visit to Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district to meet quota activist Manoj Jarange.Despite the planned visit the delegation stayed back at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar till Tuesday night. Vikhe Patil said an administrative review is being taken first before meeting Jarange. “The talks with (Jarange) are not fixed yet. We have sent him information about different demands he raised and are expecting a response from his side first,” he told reporters.Jarange, whose agitation entered the fourth day on Tuesday, refused to undergo periodic medical check-up. Jalna district collector Ashmita Mittal visited the agitation site. “We held discussion with the core committee of Maratha reservation and apprised them about our side. We held dialogue with Jarange and also inquired about his health,” she said.Jarange has been demanding immediate issuance of Kunbi certificates to all eligible Marathas. He has also appealed to the Maratha community to adopt a “guerrilla strategy” and start reaching Mumbai quietly by Sept 12. If demands are not met by then, Jarange is expected to announce the final date for his march to Mumbai.

Article Title: HC quashes FIR against in-laws accused of dowry harassment
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court has quashed and set aside the FIR and chargesheet filed by Solapur police against the in-laws who were accused by a woman of harrasment for dowry.The HC bench of justice Abhay Mantri found the similarities of the case with other cases heard and judgments of which were pronounced by the Supreme Court -- Dara Lakshmi Narayana versus State of Telangana, Geeta Mehrotra versus State of UP, and Kahkashan Kausar versus State of Bihar.The woman got married in 2017 and lived with her husband till 2021. She accused her husband and in-laws (mother, father, brothers and their wives) of demanding Rs10 lakh dowry for setting up business for one of her brothers-in-law.She also accused the in-laws of harassment and taunts about her father’s financial status. The woman alleged that they kept her hungry and picked up quarrels. She was also taken to psychiatrists “without any reason” by her husband.The in-laws had approached the HC against the FIR and chargesheet filed before the trial court. “The witnesses whose statements were recorded have not provided any details or described any particular instances of harassment by applicant Nos.2 to 7, but their statements appear vague, omnibus, and stereotypical. Therefore, they do not prima facie inspire confidence to demonstrate that applicant Nos. 2 to 7 were involved in the present crime,” stated the order passed on Aug 28.“No specific act done by applicant Nos. 2 to 7, which constitutes the offence under section 498-A of the IPC, has been mentioned. Apart from that, there is no mention of time, date, place or manner in which the alleged harassment occurred. Thus, the FIR and the entire chargesheet lack concrete and precise allegations,” the order added.The court stated that mere reference to the names of family members in a criminal case arising out of a matrimonial dispute, without specific allegations indicating their active involvement, should be nipped in the bud.“It is a well-recognized fact, borne out of judicial experience, that there is often a tendency to implicate all the members of the husband's family when domestic disputes arise out of matrimonial discord. Such generalized and sweeping accusations unsupported by concrete evidence or particularized allegations cannot form the basis for criminal prosecution. Courts must exercise caution in such cases to prevent misuse of legal provisions and the legal process and avoid unnecessarily harassing innocent family members,” the court observed in its order.
Article Summary: The Kolhapur bench of the Bombay high court has quashed and set aside the FIR and chargesheet filed by Solapur police against the in-laws. The woman got married in 2017 and lived with her husband till 2021. She accused her husband and in-law of demanding Rs10 lakh dowry for setting up business for one of her brothers-in-law.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: 3,400 SIR forms found at Navi Mumbai photocopy shop; 5 BLOs suspended as Sena (UBT)-BJP clash
Article Text:
Authorities seized numerous printed Special Intensive Revision forms from the premises

THANE/MUMBAI: Five Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were suspended after 3,400 enumeration forms related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls were found at a private photocopy shop in Navi Mumbai’s Kharghar, triggering a political confrontation between Shiv Sena (UBT) and BJP workers and prompting an administrative inquiry, police and district officials said.The forms, which were filled by voters from the Panvel Assembly constituency, were found at a photocopy centre in Sector 19 following complaints that SIR applications were being photocopied there and that a person associated with the BJP youth wing was allegedly in unauthorised possession of them.Police rushed to the shop and took Suraj Patil, who was allegedly getting the forms photocopied, into custody.Authorities also seized thousands of printed SIR forms from the premises and shifted them to the police station, news agency PTI reported.he controversy came to light after a video related to the incident went viral on Thursday.The administration subsequently ordered an inquiry into how forms filled by voters reached a private photocopy centre.Following the complaint, the Electoral Registration Officer deputed Assistant Electoral Registration Officers to inspect the photocopy centre.During the inspection, officials found that Patil had brought 3,400 applications to the shop.Scrutiny showed that the forms belonged to 11 polling stations. A majority of the applications were from five polling stations, while single copies were found from six other polling stations.Shiv Sena (UBT) workers had confronted Patil at the shop, alleging that he was a BJP Youth Wing office-bearer. BJP workers, however, denied any connection with the matter.Sena (UBT) workers also alleged that Patil managed to flee the Kharghar police station shortly after being taken there for questioning.Raigad district collector Kishan Jawale on Friday said a case had been registered against Patil under the Representation of the People Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Jawale visited the office of Panvel Sub-Divisional Officer Pawan Chandak and said the five BLOs had been suspended pending disciplinary proceedings.Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer Balesh Bhojane questioned how SIR forms filled by ordinary voters could have reached private individuals and alleged that BJP youth wing functionaries were linked to the incident.Panvel Municipal Corporation mayor and BJP leader Nitin Patil, however, said party workers had no connection with the matter.Opposition NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said suspending the five BLOs was not enough and alleged that the incident exposed problems in the way the SIR process was being conducted."We have been saying that the BJP is using this process to ensure its poll victory and this incident proves us right," he said.Pawar said he had sought a response from the Election Commission over the incident, but the authorities had passed the responsibility to the Election Commission of India."Suspending only the BLOs is not enough. The authorities who instructed them should also be suspended, and action should be taken against the BJP workers involved," Pawar added.He also said there could be many similar incidents that had not been detected and sought a response from the Election Commission.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: 5 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) suspended after 3,400 enumeration forms found at private photocopy shop in Navi Mumbai’s Kharghar. Police took Suraj Patil, who was allegedly getting the forms photocopied, into custody. Authorities also seized thousands of printed SIR forms from the premises.

Article Title: Man held for performing ‘black magic’ at crematorium
Article Text: Nagpur: Kuhi police of Nagpur rural on Wednesday arrested a 58-year-old Bhilgaon resident for allegedly performing black magic at a village crematorium and around a complainant’s house.Ramnaresh Vishwakarma, residing at Bhilgaon, was taken into custody on Sept 2 under Section 3(2) of the Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act. He was remanded in police custody till Sept 3.The complaint was lodged by Prashant Balu Chacherkar (31) of Salwa in Kuhi taluka. After performing his father’s last rites, he visited the Salwa crematorium at 9 am on Aug 25 to collect the ashes.Chacherkar found a yellow-cloth doll tied with red and yellow threads, a bottle containing liquid, lemons, and incense sticks at the spot where the last rites were performed. Clothes, socks, a pair of shoes, threads and lemons were also recovered from a nearby mourning hall. The same evening, cut lemons were placed on all four sides of Chacherkar’s house.
Article Summary: Ramnaresh Vishwakarma, residing at Bhilgaon, was taken into custody on Sept 2 under Section 3(2) of the Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and Black Magic Act. He was remanded in police custody till Sept 3.

Article Title: MCOCA slapped on Chintalwar, gang members
Article Text: Nagpur: City police have invoked Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against Sumeet Chintalwar syndicate in South Nagpur. On other hand, a gambling den linked to Rushtam and Salauddin in North Nagpur continues to draw goons from across the city.Additional commissioner of police Vasant Pardeshi on August 29 granted the approval for invoking MCOCA in the case registered at Ajni police station under the anti-narcotics law.The accused are Sumit Chintalwar (32), Aaditya Telgote (23), Karan Gatlewar (27), and Naresh Tekam (32), a native of Lamta in Balaghat, Madhya Pradesh.Pardeshi recorded that more than one charge sheet had already been filed against the gang in offences punishable with three years or more, and courts had taken cognisance. Convinced that a crime syndicate existed, Pardeshi directed the Ajni Division assistant commissioner of police to conduct an investigation under the supervision of DCP, Zone IV.
Article Summary: City police have invoked Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against Sumeet Chintalwar syndicate in South Nagpur. A gambling den linked to Rushtam and Salauddin in North Nagpur continues to draw goons from across the city.

Article Title: Congress will oppose delimitation exercise, says former CM Prithviraj Chavan
Article Text:
Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan

Nashik

:





Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan on Tuesday said Congress would oppose Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise, irrespective of whether Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) chose to support it.“Centre should avoid undertaking the exercise without broad political consensus. It should take all stakeholders into confidence before taking any decision on delimitation,” Chavan said, while speaking to reporters in Nashik ahead of Rahul Gandhi ’s visit on Wednesday.Chavan was in the city ahead of the concluding session of a 10-day training camp for Congress district presidents from Maharashtra. Gandhi is scheduled to address the closed-door programme on Wednesday at MTDC’s Grape Park Resort near Gangapur dam.Raising questions over the transparency of projects linked to the Simhastha Kumbh Mela, Chavan said Congress had sought the detailed project report (DPR) for the proposed works but had not received it so far. While supporting govt’s planned expenditure of Rs 34,000 crore on Kumbh-related infrastructure, he said the funds must be used to create durable civic assets rather than temporary facilities.“We are not opposed to spending Rs 34,000 crore on Kumbh Mela works. The investment should create permanent infrastructure and contribute to Nashik’s long-term development. Govt must also focus on accelerating the city’s industrial growth,” he said.Targeting BJP , Chavan claimed the ruling party had entered a “panic mode” following recent protests by Gen Z youth in Delhi and was increasingly concerned about the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He alleged that BJP was even considering advancing the general elections to 2028.Chavan also claimed Prime Minister Narendra Modi was facing resistance over a proposed Union cabinet reshuffle. According to him, three Union ministers, including Nitin Gadkari and Rajnath Singh, were likely to be replaced but had opposed the move.On the education front, the former CM stressed the need for a full-time Union education minister, saying the portfolio was currently being handled as an additional charge by Union minister Pralhad Joshi. “There is no Union education minister with the national stature and credibility required to engage with students and address growing concerns over the examination system,” Chavan added.
Article Summary: Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan said Congress would oppose Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise. Chavan was in the city ahead of the concluding session of a 10-day training camp for Congress district presidents from Maharashtra. Rahul Gandhi is scheduled to address the closed-door programme on Wednesday.

Article Title: Duo assault Malaysian tourists near Coimbatore
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: A Malaysian man and his son were assaulted with deadly weapons by two unidentified men following a heated altercation near a petrol outlet at Navakkarai in Coimbatore district on Wednesday evening.The injured have been identified as Loganathan, 52, and his son Ugendran,21. Both were admitted to a private hospital in Madukkarai.According to police, 11 Malaysian tourists were travelling in a hired van from Alappuzha in Kerala to Chennai. Around 5.30pm, when the vehicle stopped near a petrol pump on the Cochin–Salem Bypass, an altercation broke out between the tourists and two men on the road. The argument quickly escalated, and the duo attacked Loganathan and Ugendran with sickles, damaging the vehicle’s windowpanes.Following the assault, the driver sped towards Madukkarai. However, the assailants chased the van on a two-wheeler. Upon reaching Madukkarai market, one of the pursuers brandished an object resembling a firearm, forcing the driver to stop the vehicle. As locals rushed to the scene upon hearing the commotion, the assailants fled.Alerted by locals, the Madukkarai police and senior officers arrived at the scene. They secured CCTV footage on the bypass to identify the culprits and establish the sequence of events.Police registered a case and launched a manhunt.
Article Summary: A Malaysian man and his son were assaulted with deadly weapons by two unidentified men following a heated altercation near a petrol outlet at Navakkarai in Coimbatore district on Wednesday evening. The duo attacked Loganathan and Ugendran with sickles, damaging the vehicle’s windowpanes.

Article Title: I am constitutionally bound to accept voluntary resignation of MLA, TamilNadu assembly speaker tells Madras high court
Article Text:
J C D Prabhakar





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu assembly speaker J C D Prabhakar on Tuesday informed the Madras high court that he is constitutionally duty bound to accept the resignation tendered by an MLA if it is done voluntarily. No one can compel a legislator to continue in his/her post, he said.Senior advocate C S Vaidyanathan and advocate-general Vijay Narayan made the submission on behalf of the speaker while opposing the pleas challenging his decision in accepting the resignation of six AIADMK MLAs before deciding the disqualification proceedings for cross voting in favour of the TVK govt violating party whip.Recording the submissions, the first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan reserved their orders. The petitions were filed by AIADMK whip Agri S S Krishnamurthy and others.Acceptance of the resignations would not automatically render the pending disqualification proceedings ineffective. If an MLA wishes to resign, he or she cannot be compelled to continue in office. Refusal to accept such resignations would amount to a failure on the part of the speaker to discharge a constitutional duty, Vaidyanathan said.“The speaker could inquire only whether the resignations were submitted voluntarily.The other aspects of whether the MLAs resigned in exchange for a ministerial position or money, or whether horse-trading had taken place, could be examined only as part of the disqualification proceedings,” he added.The purpose or motive behind a resignation could not be examined while deciding whether to accept it, he said.Representing the MLAs, senior advocates Satish Parasaran and Menaka Guruswamy contended that defection proceedings would arise only if an MLA continued to enjoy the privileges of office while extending support to another political party. Resigning from the office of MLA and subsequently joining another political party constitute democratic political activity, they said.Senior counsel V V Giri and S R Rajagopal for Krishnamurthy submitted that conducting an inquiry to ascertain whether the resignations were made voluntarily or not was not merely a procedural formality but a constitutional obligation, and that no meaningful inquiry had actually been conducted.
Article Summary: No one can compel a legislator to continue in his/her post, he said. The purpose or motive behind a resignation could not be examined while deciding whether to accept it. The petitions were filed by AIADMK whip Agri S S Krishnamurthy and others.

Article Title: Pay aid dues to victim of HIV blood transfusion: HC
Article Text:
Madras high court on Wednesday directed the state to pay pending arrears of financial assistance to the victim woman who was transfused HIV-infected blood while she was pregnant, at a govt hospital in Sattur in Virudhunagar district in 2018.





Madurai: Madras high court on Wednesday directed the state to pay pending arrears of financial assistance to the victim woman who was transfused HIV-infected blood while she was pregnant, at a govt hospital in Sattur in Virudhunagar district in 2018.A division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel passed the order while hearing a batch of petitions seeking a direction to the state to provide compensation to the woman.Earlier, the court had directed the state to pay Rs25 lakh compensation and provide her govt employment. It was also directed to provide monthly financial assistance of Rs7,500 to the woman. The court further directed the state to construct a house and provide a two-wheeler to her. The hearing in the batch of petitions was adjourned to Sept 17.
Article Summary: Madras high court on Wednesday directed the state to pay pending arrears of financial assistance to the victim woman. The woman was transfused HIV-infected blood while she was pregnant, at a govt hospital in Sattur in Virudhunagar district in 2018. The court also directed to provide monthly financial assistance of Rs7,500 to the woman.

Article Title: Two arrested with 100 tapentadol tablets in Madurai
Article Text:
City police arrested two men on Tuesday for allegedly possessing and selling tapentadol tablets.

Madurai

:





City police arrested two men on Tuesday for allegedly possessing and selling tapentadol tablets.Acting on a tip-off, police conducted surveillance in the Rathinapuri area on Monday. When officers attempted to intercept an autorickshaw, its occupants allegedly abandoned the vehicle and fled on noticing the police team.Police searched the autorickshaw and recovered 100 tapentadol tablets concealed beneath the driver’s seat. Sellur police registered a case and launched an investigation to trace those involved. Following enquiries, police arrested Vinodh Kumar, 29, of Palanganatham, and Aaron Edison, 28, of Narimedu, on Tuesday.Both were later remanded in judicial custody.

Article Title: Cop held for bludgeoning woman to death
Article Text:
A 32-year-old police constable attached to Thattarmadam station in Thoothukudi district was arrested on Tuesday for murdering a woman in Mudivaithanenthal village following a dispute linked to an alleged extramarital relationship.





Thoothukudi: A 32-year-old police constable attached to Thattarmadam station in Thoothukudi district was arrested on Tuesday for murdering a woman in Mudivaithanenthal village following a dispute linked to an alleged extramarital relationship.Police said the accused, Muthukumaran, had extramarital relations with Subbulakshmi, a widow from the village. The deceased, Priya , 39, her younger sister, opposed it and warned her sister against continuing it.On Tuesday evening, he went to the photo copy centre run by Priya and, under the influence of alcohol, picked a quarrel with her. He attacked her with an iron rod, inflicting multiple injuries to her face, and fled. Priya died on the spot, police said.Police shifted the body to the medical college hospital for postmortem. A case was registered at Pudukottai police station under Section 103(1) of BNS, and the accused was arrested. Police said Muthukumaran had also figured in an earlier assault case. Departmental action is being initiated against him while further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Police said the accused, Muthukumaran, had extramarital relations with Subbulakshmi, a widow from the village. The deceased, Priya, 39, her younger sister, opposed it and warned her sister against continuing it. He went to the photo copy centre run by Priya and, under the influence of alcohol, picked a quarrel with her.

Article Title: Two women killed as car rams bike near Srivaikuntam in Thoothukudi
Article Text:
Two women killed as car rams bike near Srivaikuntam in Thoothukudi





Thoothukudi: Two women were killed after a car rammed into the two-wheeler they were travelling on near Mudivaithanenthal in Thoothukudi district on Tuesday.Police identified the deceased as Sathya , 40, of Thiruvalluvar Colony, and Amutha, 45, of Nazareth. Police said the duo were riding to Srivaikuntam on the Thoothukudi-Srivaikuntam road. When they were nearing the Mudivaithanendal tank, a speeding car rammed into the two-wheeler from behind. Both women suffered severe head injuries and died on the spot, police said.Police sent the bodies to a govt hospital for postmortem examination. They registered a case against the car driver, Saravanan , 31, of Nazareth, and arrested him. Further investigation is on.
Article Summary: Two women killed as car rams bike near Srivaikuntam in Thoothukudi district. Police identified the deceased as Sathya, 40, and Amutha, 45, of Nazareth. Both women suffered severe head injuries and died on the spot, police said.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.
